expectations.text: Preserves 18 nurses, four weeks, one clinic, and voluntary participation.
expectations.evidence: “A voluntary four-week pilot at one clinic” and “Among 18 participating nurses” retain the design and sample.

expectations.text: Preserves median weekly 46 to 39 minutes with no causal claim and explains no control plus concurrent staffing changes.
expectations.evidence: “median weekly scheduling time fell from 46 to 39 minutes”; “Without a control group, that change cannot be attributed to the tool; concurrent staffing changes may explain part of it.”

expectations.text: States six of nine survey respondents preferred it rather than six of 18 or a majority of all nurses.
expectations.evidence: “Nine nurses completed the optional survey, and six of those nine preferred the tool”; adds that this does not establish preference among all participants or elsewhere.

expectations.text: States patient safety was not measured; any next step is framed as recommendation, not a planned commitment.
expectations.evidence: “The pilot did not measure patient safety.” “Before expanding adoption, run a longer evaluation” is a recommendation, not a promised project.

expectations.text: 100–150 words in one paragraph without heading or bullets.
expectations.evidence: 112 whitespace-delimited words, one paragraph, no heading or bullets.

review_method: Independent single blind agent review; not human feedback
